claim: In benchmark testing (H100 GPU pods, vLLM v1, 10 Llama2 replicas, ShareGPT dataset, 100-1000 QPS), the Endpoint Selection Extension delivered throughput roughly on par with a standard Kubernetes Service but showed significantly lower p90 per-output-token and end-to-end latency at QPS beyond 400-500.
stance_target: GIE's metrics-aware endpoint selection materially improves tail latency over plain Kubernetes Service load balancing under high load
scope_conditions: GIE project benchmark, H100 80GB GPU pods, vLLM v1, Llama2 model, ShareGPT dataset, 100-1000 QPS via Latency Profile Generator tool
quoted_support: Comparable Throughput: Throughout the tested QPS range, the ESE delivered throughput roughly on par with a standard Kubernetes Service. Per-Output-Token Latency: The ESE showed significantly lower p90 latency at higher QPS (500+)... Overall p90 Latency: ...particularly as traffic increased beyond 400-500 QPS.
